newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - March 4.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - March 4.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

The Australia and New Zealand (ANZ) Banking Group Ltd would restructure its Esanda financing unit into two different areas and lay off a significant number of staff, an ANZ spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

News Corp and Japan's Softbank Corp said on Monday they were giving up their stake in Asahi National Broadcasting television network to one of the network's Japanese parents. But they said that in return they had secured the cooperation of a major Japanese media conglomerate for their Japan Sky Broadcasting Co, or JSkyB, a digital satellite TV project with Sony Corp which will start beaming digital channels in Japan in April.

Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd chief executive officer Neil Gamble said on Monday he expected to get a long awaited tax break for high spending gamblers from the New South Wales (NSW) government soon. Earlier the Casino said that daily attendances and revenue were up during the first two months of calendar 1997. It also reported a net loss of A$4.82 million for the 18 months ended December 31, 1996, compared with a loss of A$52.30 million for the 12 months ended June 30, 1995.

Crown Ltd said on Monday it was not interested in acquiring the troubled Reef Casino at Cairns in north Queensland state. Crown chairman Lloyd Williams, who is also Hudson Conway chief executive, said also that Hudson Conway's joint A$2 billion plan with Lend Lease Corp Ltd to develop Melbourne's Docklands district was being made on an all-or-nothing basis.

Southcorp is expected to post a sharply higher first half net profit of A$70 million. National Foods is expected to post a flat A$12.5 million first half net profit. Pacific BBA also expected to report its full year result.
Ridley Corp posted a net first profit of A$10.94 million late on Monday, down from A$11.95 million a year earlier.

Niugini Mining reported an annual net loss of A$38.91 million late on Monday, versus a A$5.02 million profit in 1995. The loss included an abnormal loss of A$24.32 million due to writedowns in its Chilean operations.
